Trump Announces New AI Leadership For ‘Super Intelligence Force’

‘The risk of not being first is high’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

President Donald Trump has handed the nation’s top intelligence official command of a new federal body built to steer American policy on artificial intelligence.

Trump announced the Super Intelligence Force (SIF) on Sunday and named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to run it, according to a post on Truth Social. The group will answer directly to the president and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, according to the post.

Clayton will share leadership with Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote. Clayton steps in as the administration’s AI czar. (RELATED: Trump Accord Enshrines Light-Touch Regulation of AI)

The task force has 120 days to deliver a report on the technology’s risks and benefits and to define the government’s role, according to a Wall Street Journal interview with Clayton.
